title: P0 apex latency surge debrief + runbook sketch
content:
Summary:

This doc captures an immediate debrief and an initial runbook sketch for the P0 latency surge that impacted hosted-api streaming and sync text endpoints on 2026-05-20 (UTC). Primary visible impact: p95/p99 latency spike and intermittent 5xx for ~27 minutes across multiple regions, with degraded streaming fragment reassembly for some sessions.

Severity: P0 (customer-facing errors + broad latency impact)
Incident window: 2026-05-20 03:12 UTC -> 2026-05-20 03:39 UTC
Impacted surfaces: hosted-api (streaming), non-stream text generation routes for medium-length requests (seq len 256-1024).
Estimated customer impact: ~6.4% of active connections experienced >2x TTFB, ~1.1% saw transient 5xx. High impact for streaming clients using multiplexed connections (mobile/web live apps).

How we detected it:
- Synthetic p95/p99 probes firing from Datadog dashboards tripped at 03:14 UTC (alert: hostedapi-p99-latency-surge).
- On-call (pager) at 03:16 UTC. Slack: #oncall-hosted-api.
- Early telemetry showed a tight correlation between increased token-estimation variance and request batching size.

Initial hypothesis (triage minutes):
- New tokenizer micro-upgrade (runtime PR 4385) changed the tokenization boundary for some requests causing token_count underestimation for ~1% of input shapes.
- Adaptive batching layer uses token_count to size batches; underestimation caused aggressive coalescing of heterogeneous sequences -> head-of-line blocking inside scheduler -> per-session streaming fragmentation and delayed start-of-stream chunks.
- Batching-induced backlog then tripped an internal per-acceptor queue threshold, triggering short-lived connection failures (5xx) as new acceptor logic returned 503 for overloaded ephemeral threads.

Timeline (consolidated):
- 03:08 UTC: Runtime PR 4385 (tokenizer tweak) promoted to canary in dedicated infra (rolling deploy to 5% edge).
- 03:12 UTC: Datadog p99 probes begin to deviate. Spike visible in region-us-west1 first.
- 03:14 UTC: Pager fires. On-call @aisha investigates.
- 03:15 UTC: Telemetry shows batching window sizes increased and KV cache eviction rate rose ~3x for affected shards.
- 03:18 UTC: Streaming chunk reassembly error rate rises ~0.9% (observability alert).
- 03:21 UTC: Mitigation - rollback tokenizer change at runtime PR level for canary hosts.
- 03:24 UTC: Partial improvement; p95 reduces but p99 still elevated.
- 03:26 UTC: Manual throttle engaged on adaptive batching (feature flag: adaptive-batching-window) for affected clusters.
- 03:30 UTC: Acceptable recovery on most shards; continued monitoring.
- 03:39 UTC: Metrics return to baseline; incident declared mitigated.

Root cause analysis (initial):
- Root cause chain: token_count misestimation (tokenizer change) -> adaptive batching mis-sizing -> scheduler head-of-line blocking -> queue buildup -> acceptor-level overload -> transient 5xx and streaming fragmentation.
- Contributing factors:
  - Lack of offline gated test for tokenization distribution shifts relative to batching heuristics.
  - Adaptive batching had limited defensive caps for heterogeneous coalescing across sequence lengths.
  - Acceptors returned overload 503 quickly under queue pressure; the backpressure/exponential-backoff path didn't sufficiently shed load gracefully, amplifying failures.

Why the tokenizer change made it worse:
- The tokenization tweak reduced token counts for a narrow class of inputs with long emoji sequences and non-latin punctuation. For those requests, runtime inferred that sequences were shorter and coalesced them with longer sequences in the same batch. When the longer sequence arrived later, the scheduler waited to complete the batch causing early sequences to stall mid-stream.

Immediate mitigations taken (on-call chronology):
- 03:21 UTC: Rolled back the tokenizer canary (runtime configuration rollback). Owner: Marco Chen.
- 03:26 UTC: Feature flag flip: adaptive-batching-window -> conservative (reduce max batch size and disable heterogenous coalescing). Owner: Priya Kapoor.
- 03:27 UTC: Temporarily relax acceptor overload threshold to allow degraded acceptance instead of 503. Owner: SRE on-call (Aisha).
- Quick comms: posted incident summary to #incident-postmortems and customer-facing ops-run via CS.

Customer communication notes:
- CS: drafted short note explaining brief degraded streaming experience in US region; no data loss; root cause under investigation.
- Follow-up required: prepare postmortem-ready customer timeline and RCA for affected enterprise customers. Owner: Diego Alvarez (CS).

Runbook sketch (actions to standardize for similar future incidents):
- Detection queries (what to run immediately):
  - p95/p99 latency by route, by region, by model_version.
  - batching window size distribution over last 10m (histogram).
  - token_count distribution delta vs baseline (per model).
  - KV cache eviction rate and lease churn.
  - streaming fragment reassembly error rate and per-session chunk latencies.

- Triage checklist (quick steps):
  1) Confirm alerts and map to regions/routes.
  2) Check recent deploys (runtime, tokenizer, batching) within last 60m.
  3) If tokenizer/runtime deploy found -> flip canary rollback on affected pools.
  4) Flip adaptive-batching-window -> conservative mode (feature flag) to reduce heterogeneous coalescing.
  5) If acceptor 503 counts rising -> increase acceptor queue cap or relax overload return threshold; as last resort, burst additional ephemeral capacity.
  6) If streaming fragment errors > threshold -> force per-session fragmentation fallback (smaller chunk sizes) and disable multiplexing on affected edges.

- Playbook commands (examples):
  - /deploy rollback runtime-canary --pool=canary-us-west1
  - curl -XPOST $ADMIN_ENDPOINT/flags/adaptive-batching-window -d '{"mode":"conservative"}'
  - ssh to acceptor-proxy -> write /proc/sys/net/acceptor/overload_thresh = 0.85 (temporary)
  - API to edge: /edges/*/set-multiplex=false (for region-scoped mitigation)

Monitoring & Alerts to add or refine:
- New alert: token-count-drift-by-model (>2 sigma) triggers internal review before rolling tokenizer runtime changes to canary.
- Alert: batching-window-heterogeneity (ratio of median to 95th pct batch sizes) -> early signal for mis-coalescing.
- SLO telemetry: add streaming-chunk-start latency SLI with p99 thresholds, separate from overall TTFB.

Longer-term fixes (action items):
- Engineering: Add tokenization distribution unit tests that run against adaptive batching heuristics in CI (owner: runtime team, Marco). Due: 2026-06-15.
- Engineering: Add hard caps for heterogeneous coalescing in adaptive batcher and a fallback to per-request scheduling if variance exceeds threshold. (owner: serving-runtime, Priya). Due: 2026-06-22.
- SRE: Implement new alert for token-count-drift and pre-deploy gating for tokenizer changes. (owner: eng-sre, Aisha). Due: 2026-05-30.
- Product/Devexp: Update deployment checklist to include synthetic probes that mirror new tokenization shapes (owner: DevEx, Diego). Due: 2026-06-05.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Exact token shapes that triggered worst underestimation — need sample set sanitized and attached to JIRA-SRE-2119. (action: runtime team).
- Should adaptive batcher prefer time-window-first policy for streaming sessions to avoid head-of-line blocking? Evaluate trade-offs. (action: design doc).
- How often do tokenizer micro-upgrades shift distribution in production? Consider automated drift tests.

On-call notes (raw):
- 03:16 - @aisha: saw p99 spike, started checking deploy pipeline -> found PR 4385 had rolled to canary at 03:08.
- 03:17 - Slack snippet: "marco can you confirm tokenizer canary? seeing weird batching histograms"
- 03:20 - Marco: "rolling back canary now"
- 03:25 - Priya flips adaptive-batching-window -> conservative. Immediate partial relief.
- 03:28 - Acceptors still returning 503 for a short window -> increased queue cap; 503 count drops.
- 03:33 - Metrics trending down. 
- Note: debugging was noisy due to overlapping maintenance jobs; recommend a short freeze window on unrelated infra work when investigating P0.

Post-incident comms plan (draft):
- Internal: detailed RCA and timeline to #incident-postmortems within 48h. Owner: Aisha.
- Customer-facing: timeline + mitigation summary for affected customers within 72h. Owner: Diego.
- Engineering write-up: root cause analysis and design doc for adaptive batching changes. Owner: Priya + Marco.

Appendix: quick diagnostic queries (copied for runbook)
- SELECT count(*) FROM batches WHERE window_size > 2*median AND model='x' AND ts > now()-10m;
- host_metrics:batch_window_histogram{region="us-west1"}.rollup(1m)
- streaming_errors{type="fragment_reassembly"}.rollup(1m)

Notes to self (informal):
- This felt like a classic "small upstream change + brittle downstream heuristic" problem. Need stronger pre-canary signals that exercise the heuristics.
- Good cross-team coordination; rollback + conservative batching was the right immediate combo.
- Keep the runbook lean and add command snippets so junior on-call can act fast.

-- end of draft --
